title: Spike a 500 ml saline bag with an infusion giving set, keeping the spike sterile
instruction: Spike the saline bag with the giving set, keeping the spike sterile, and leave the bag on the tray.
context: Every gravity infusion starts with a bag spiked by a giving set, routine work many times a shift for registered nurses (3,175,390 US jobs) and licensed practical nurses (630,250; BLS, May 2023). The port's protector must be torn off, the spike uncapped and pushed firmly through the port's diaphragm, and the bare spike must touch nothing but the port's opened end, or the set is thrown away.
setup: A station table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A smooth stainless-steel tray, fixed: 34 x 54 cm, 4 mm thick, from 16 to 50 cm forward and from 30 cm right to 24 cm left of the centre line; soft PVC grips it at a friction of 0.45 (0.40 sliding). (2) A full 500 ml bag of 0.9 % sodium chloride, clear PVC, lying flat along the left-right line, its ports toward the right arm: 13.0 x 22.5 cm with its welded seams (1 mm thick; the top seam 2.5 cm wide with a hanger hole); the filled pillow 11.5 x 18.5 cm and 3.0 cm thick with rounded long sides (602 ml inside), holding 540 ml of saline (makers overfill 500 ml bags) and about 30 ml of air; 570 g in all (543 g of saline, 27 g of film, ports and protector). The pillow's middle is 31.4 cm forward and 9.5 cm left of the centre line; a white label with a 100 ml scale on top. (3) At the bag's bottom seam, 1.25 cm right of the centre line, two 8 mm PVC ports along the left-right line, their axes 1.5 cm above the tray: the spike port 29.6 cm forward, 36 mm long, its mouth 4.85 cm right of the centre line, with a diaphragm 10 mm inside its mouth; and the medication port with a grey rubber plug, 33.2 cm forward, 20 mm long. (4) On the spike port's outer 26 mm, its blue polyethylene tamper-evident protector (3 g): a sleeve 11 mm across and 25 mm long, closed 2 mm past the mouth, with a flat pull tab 16 x 12 x 2 mm. (5) A gravity infusion giving set lying on the tray along the left-right line, its spike pointing left, its axis 1 cm above the tray at 41 cm forward: a white ABS spike 5.6 mm across and 24 mm long from its flange (16 mm across) to its point, the flange's face 9.5 cm right of the centre line; over the spike a white polyethylene cap 10 mm across and 30 mm long with two fins (2 g); behind the flange a hub with an air vent, a clear PVC drip chamber 20 mm across and 60 mm long (empty), its outlet, and 10 cm of 4.1 mm PVC line with a blue roller clamp (16 x 45 x 14 mm); 25 g without the cap (about a whole set's weight; the rest of its 1.8 m line is left out). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0.0 if the spike, once its cap has started to come off, ever touches anything but the port's opened end, the 26 mm its protector covered (latched): the tray, the table, the bag's film, seams, port base or medication port, the protector, or, once the cap is fully off, the cap or either gripper. Otherwise judged at the end: 1.0 with the spike in the port up to its flange (the flange within 1.5 mm of the port's mouth), the bag lying on the tray (its middle over the tray, its underside within 1 cm of it, tilted under 15 degrees) and neither gripper touching the bag or the giving set; 0.75 with the spike in the port up to its flange; 0.5 with the spike through the port's diaphragm (more than 11 mm in); 0.25 with the port's protector torn off; else 0.0. Real trial: the same rules, measured so: touches of the bare spike judged frame by frame from the video, as an assessor marks aseptic non-touch technique; the flange-to-mouth gap with a caliper (1.5 mm or less: seated; under 13 mm: through the diaphragm, which a squeeze of the bag confirms when saline drips into the chamber); the torn tamper seal by inspection; the bag on the tray and the hands off it from the last frames. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the bag, the giving set, the protector, the cap and both arms still.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX, 240 Hz). The full bag is one rigid 570 g pillow; a real one gives a little, and its port bends. No liquid is simulated: the chamber is not primed and no fill level is scored. The protector's seal and the spike's cap are slide joints that let go at 10 N and 4 N. The spike enters the port's end without colliding; a slide joint caught at the mouth is the bore: a 20 N diaphragm, then a 3 N grip. Twisting does not help. Spike touches are PhysX contacts.
